limitations: This create-only request is an explicit closure over the discovery assignment; an empty reviewer_added_requests array means no reviewer-added candidates were found.
Ranking evidence and candidate material fingerprints are copied exactly from the bound discovery capsule and do not replace final source review.

reviewer_added_requests.discovery_reason: Architecture-enforcement-tooling chooses deterministic checks, CI placement, generated-code exceptions, and dependency gates, while build-tool-professional-usage owns build graph edges, generated authority, toolchain identity, and reproducibility. Full material is required to determine when an enforcement choice crosses into a build-graph decision and which skill owns its proof.

Configuration-runtime-policy owns typed configuration, defaults, flags, rollout, rollback, and cleanup, while secret-configuration-security owns sensitive-config exposure, access, rotation, revocation, and redaction. Full material is required to verify the general-config versus secret-lifecycle handoff and prevent security-sensitive configuration from being closed by the generic policy skill.

Extensibility-design owns plugin and hook contracts, compatibility, deprecation, isolation, and retirement, while sdk-library-contract-design owns consumed public library surfaces, generated lineage, mixed-version adoption, and consumer proof. The lightweight boundary cannot determine when a host extension contract is also a public SDK or library contract, so full candidate material is required.

High-risk-design-review is selected for a major architecture boundary and returns design findings and residual risk, while architecture-impact-reviewer returns the specialized placement decision, architecture verdict, and structural risk. Full material is required to establish the delegation boundary and prevent a broad high-risk review from substituting for the architecture-specific verdict.

Layered-architecture-design owns layer responsibilities, dependency direction, adapters, and cross-cutting placement, while dependency-wiring-lifecycle owns composition authority, lifetime scope, reusable resources, startup, shutdown, and override fidelity. Full material is required to distinguish an architectural layer violation from a construction or lifecycle wiring decision at the same dependency edge.

Microservice-splitting explicitly requires transaction boundaries to be redesigned when data ownership crosses a new service boundary, while transaction-consistency owns transaction scope, isolation, conflicts, and proving tests. Full material is required to verify that a split assessment routes the consistency decision instead of merely naming a Saga, outbox, compensation, or reconciliation mechanism.

Module-boundary-design derives public and private surfaces from verified consumers, failures, compatibility, and versioning needs, while sdk-library-contract-design owns consumed library APIs, semantic compatibility, generated lineage, adoption, and release handoffs. Full material is required to determine when an owner-controlled module surface becomes an externally consumed SDK or library contract.

Technology-stack-selection compares hard constraints, feasible commitments, total-change cost, coexistence, reversibility, and exit, while architecture-tradeoff-analysis owns architecture-wide option consequences and assumption-change triggers. Because the target explicitly routes architecture-wide ADR work to this candidate, full material is required to define the stack-specific versus architecture-wide comparison boundary.
